note: its own Grundrecht (B2 Unit 20) in Germany's Grundgesetz, distinct from B2 Unit 13's die Meinungsfreiheit — protecting artistic expression specifically.

examples.de: Die Kunstfreiheit ist im deutschen Grundgesetz eigens geschützt.
examples.en: Freedom of art is specifically protected in the German Basic Law.

note: "öffentliche Kulturförderung" — public money supporting theatres, museums, and artists, a recurring budget debate.

examples.de: Die Kulturförderung wurde im neuen Haushalt gekürzt.
examples.en: Arts funding was cut in the new budget.

note: the general economic term; die Kulturförderung is essentially a Subvention aimed specifically at the arts.

examples.de: Ohne staatliche Subventionen könnten viele Theater nicht überleben.
examples.en: Without state subsidies, many theatres couldn't survive.

note: the verb behind die Subvention — "ein Projekt subventionieren".

examples.de: Der Staat subventioniert kleine Kulturprojekte auf dem Land.
examples.en: The state subsidises small cultural projects in rural areas.

note: "ein gesellschaftskritischer Roman/Film" — art that directly examines or challenges social conditions.

examples.de: Ihr neuer Roman gilt als scharf gesellschaftskritisch.
examples.en: Her new novel is considered sharply socially critical.

note: "Kulturhauptstadt Europas" — a yearly EU title given to a city, often boosting Kulturförderung and tourism there.

examples.de: Die Stadt wurde zur Kulturhauptstadt Europas ernannt.
examples.en: The city was named European Capital of Culture.

note: "unter Denkmalschutz stehen" — legal protection for historically significant buildings and sites, distinct from B1's broader die Kulturerbe (cultural heritage as a concept).

examples.de: Das alte Rathaus steht unter Denkmalschutz.
examples.en: The old town hall is under heritage protection.

note: a broader intellectual tradition of critiquing culture and society itself — not the same as a simple Rezension (review) of one artwork.

examples.de: Die Kulturkritik dieser Zeit richtete sich vor allem gegen den Konsum.
examples.en: The cultural criticism of this period was directed mainly against consumerism.

note: art and artists that push boundaries ahead of mainstream taste — often the origin of later gesellschaftskritisch movements.

examples.de: Die Avantgarde der 1920er Jahre brach radikal mit alten Formen.
examples.en: The avant-garde of the 1920s radically broke with old forms.

note: a critical term (associated with Adorno) for culture mass-produced and marketed like any other commodity — contrasted with art as independent expression.

examples.de: Kritiker sprechen von einer Kulturindustrie, die Kunst zur Ware macht.
examples.en: Critics speak of a culture industry that turns art into a commodity.

note: using elements of another culture, often without permission or context — a frequent, contested topic in art criticism today.

examples.de: Der Vorwurf der kulturellen Aneignung sorgte für eine hitzige Debatte.
examples.en: The accusation of cultural appropriation sparked a heated debate.

note: political and cultural activity organised around group identity — a term used both descriptively and, often, critically.

examples.de: Über den Begriff Identitätspolitik wird kontrovers diskutiert.
examples.en: The term identity politics is discussed controversially.

english: the cultural sector, the arts scene (as an institution)
note: "im Kulturbetrieb arbeiten" — the whole system of theatres, galleries, funding bodies, and institutions, not just individual artists.

examples.de: Der Kulturbetrieb wurde durch die Pandemie schwer getroffen.
examples.en: The cultural sector was hit hard by the pandemic.

note: private individuals or companies funding art — an older alternative or complement to state die Kulturförderung.

examples.de: Ohne privates Mäzenatentum hätten viele Künstler früherer Jahrhunderte nicht arbeiten können.
examples.en: Without private patronage, many artists of earlier centuries couldn't have worked.

note: "ein provokantes Kunstwerk" — art that deliberately unsettles or challenges its audience.

examples.de: Das Kunstwerk wurde als bewusst provokant beschrieben.
examples.en: The artwork was described as deliberately provocative.

note: "kontrovers diskutiert werden" — often paired with provokant, but focused on generating disagreement rather than just unsettling.

examples.de: Die Ausstellung wurde in den Medien kontrovers diskutiert.
examples.en: The exhibition was discussed controversially in the media.

note: applies B2 Unit 15's die Zensur to this unit's subject — a work removed or banned, often clashing directly with die Kunstfreiheit.

examples.de: Der Fall löste eine Debatte über Zensur in der Kunst aus.
examples.en: The case sparked a debate about censorship of art.

note: a more everyday, less legally precise near-synonym of die Kunstfreiheit — used in casual discussion rather than legal argument.

examples.de: Der Regisseur verteidigte seine künstlerische Freiheit.
examples.en: The director defended his artistic freedom.

note: "Teil des öffentlichen Diskurses werden" — the broader public conversation a controversial artwork can trigger.

examples.de: Der Film wurde schnell Teil des öffentlichen Diskurses.
examples.en: The film quickly became part of the public discourse.

note: a specific, often physical object or site of cultural value — narrower than B1's broader das Kulturerbe (heritage as a whole concept).

examples.de: Das Gemälde gilt als nationales Kulturgut.
examples.en: The painting is considered a national cultural asset.

english: restitution (returning looted or stolen cultural property)
note: "die Restitution von Kulturgütern" — a major current debate, especially around colonial-era museum collections.

examples.de: Die Restitution kolonialer Kulturgüter wird zunehmend gefordert.
examples.en: The restitution of colonial-era cultural property is increasingly being demanded.

note: the historical context behind many Restitution debates — how much of what's in Western museums was acquired under colonial rule.

examples.de: Die Aufarbeitung des Kolonialismus prägt die aktuelle Museumsdebatte.
examples.en: Reckoning with colonialism shapes the current museum debate.

note: "mehr Repräsentation fordern" — whether and how different groups appear in film, literature, and museums.

examples.de: Viele fordern mehr Repräsentation marginalisierter Gruppen im Film.
examples.en: Many are calling for more representation of marginalised groups in film.

note: the commercial side — buying, selling, and pricing art — often discussed in tension with art's cultural or critical value.

examples.de: Der Kunstmarkt erzielt für manche Werke Rekordpreise.
examples.en: The art market achieves record prices for some works.

english: cultural participation, equitable access to culture
note: the policy-level concern that everyone, regardless of income or background, should be able to take part in cultural life — deepens B1's plain verb "teilnehmen".

examples.de: Kulturelle Teilhabe darf nicht vom Einkommen abhängen.
examples.en: Cultural participation shouldn't depend on income.

note: "als elitär kritisiert werden" — a common criticism aimed at Hochkultur (B1) institutions that feel closed off to most people.

examples.de: Die Oper wird von manchen als elitär wahrgenommen.
examples.en: The opera is perceived by some as elitist.

english: art as a mirror of society
note: a common framing for why art matters beyond entertainment — it reflects, questions, and sometimes shapes the society that produces it.

examples.de: Man sagt oft, Kunst sei ein Spiegel der Gesellschaft.
examples.en: It's often said that art is a mirror of society.

english: review — culture as leisure vs. culture as a social force
note: B1 Unit 24 gave you culture as something you consume in your free time — Ausstellung, Veranstaltung, Eintritt. This unit gives you culture as something that funds debates, gets censored, gets fought over, and shapes society.

examples.de: Erst der Museumsbesuch, dann die Frage nach der Restitution.
examples.en: First the museum visit, then the question of restitution.
